prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1201; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers were dispatched to a two-vehicle collision on a Houston, Texas roadway where a low-speed head-on impact had occurred between the two vehicles. Driver 1 was operating the first vehicle, which was registered to and insured under the policy held by Driver 1. Driver 2 was operating the second vehicle. A Passenger was also seated in the first vehicle at the time of impact. Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder and was evaluated at the scene. The reported injury is consistent with the mechanism of a collision of this kind. Witnesses at the scene, photographs taken by responding personnel, and statements from Driver 2 all corroborate the account of how the collision occurred. Both officers and witnesses confirmed that Driver 1 was inside the vehicle when the impact took place. Damage to the front of the first vehicle and the rear of the second is largely consistent with the described impact. Some older scratches were noted on the first vehicle's bumper, which may predate this collision and were recorded for reference only.
